LAST TIME: The Maharal returns to Prague, and makes many improvements in the community. However, because he is unafraid to rebuke the rich and powerful, he also makes some enemies. These enemies oppose the idea of the Maharal being appointed as chief rabbi, some even spreading false rumors about him. The Fierce Leader

lashon hara, it is as serious as the three most severe aveiros: avoda zara, adultery, and murder.’ Lashon

hara is an aveira done with speech. Speech is the power that is unique to the human being. It’s what sets people apart from all other animals, and makes us special. Speaking lashon hara brings tum’ah into this unique power of speech, which is why it has such serious consequences.

“Unfortunately, many in our generation ignore the severity of this aveira. They spread evil lies and insults against holy and righteous people, slandering them with the insulting nickname, ‘nadler’.” The Maharal thumped a fist on the bima as he said a final sentence: “This cannot go on!”

With that, the Maharal stepped down from the podium, and went over to the aron kodesh. He gripped the gold and red-velvet paroches in his right hand, and turned to face the people. “Great poskim before us, the Maharam and the Avi Ha’ezri, have declared a cherem against those who speak lashon hara. Today we will reinforce their words, and add our own.” Then the Maharal pulled back the paroches. He called up ten dayanim, rabbanim and roshei yeshiva and gave them each a sefer Torah to hold.

holy congregation of Prague, with the power of the kedusha vested in these sifrei Torah, we hereby declare a cherem against anyone who spreads slander and lies, and against anyone who uses the insult ‘nadler’ against any fellow Jew.”

Shabbos morning, and he didn’t budge later on, when the city council voted and decided against appointing the Maharal as chief rabbi. On the contrary, the Maharal felt he would be able to serve the Jews of Prague better if he didn’t have to deal with the politics involved with being in that official role.

And serve his community he did. Over the years, the Maharal’s brilliance and integrity earned him respect in the eyes of both Jews and non-Jews around Prague. In fact, his reputation grew so much over the years that the new emperor, Rudolph II4, became intrigued.
